title: Place a square root on the number line
summary: Build a right triangle and swing the slanted side onto the line to see where the square root of k sits.
alt: A right triangle with legs sqrt(k-1) and 1. Its hypotenuse sqrt(k) is swung onto the number line.

leg.label: Base
leg.text: The side along the number line.

hyp.label: Square root
hyp.text: The hypotenuse, swung onto the line.

steps.title: Draw a number line
steps.narration: We want to **see** \( \sqrt{2} \) as a point on the number line. Start with the points 0 and 1.

steps.title: Build a right triangle
steps.narration: At 1, stand a segment of length **1** straight up. The triangle has two sides of length 1 and a right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras gives the slanted side
steps.narration: The slanted side is \( \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2} \). It is the [[hyp|hypotenuse]], and it has length \( \sqrt{2} \).

steps.title: Swing it down
steps.narration: Put the compass point on 0 and swing the hypotenuse down onto the line. It lands at \( \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414 \). Now \( \sqrt{2} \) has an exact place on the number line.

steps.title: Keep going: root 3
steps.narration: Use that new length \( \sqrt{2} \) as the base and 1 as the height: \( \sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{3} \). Swing again and you reach \( \sqrt{3} \).

steps.title: Any square root
steps.narration: Each new triangle adds 1 under the root: \( \sqrt{4}, \sqrt{5}, \ldots \). Drag **k** to place any \( \sqrt{k} \) yourself.

formulas.title: Hypotenuse
formulas.text: A base of √(k−1) and a height of 1 give a hypotenuse of √k.

challenges.title: Find the slanted side
challenges.prompt: Base \( \sqrt{8} \), height 1. How long is the hypotenuse?
challenges.hint: Square the base, add 1, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Where does it land?
challenges.prompt: Where on the number line does \( \sqrt{5} \) land?

challenges.title: Is it exact?

options.label: Yes, a real point on the line
No, it is only an approximation

challenges.prompt: Is the point P in the picture exactly \( \sqrt{2} \)?
challenges.hint: The compass swings an exact length.
challenges.explain: The length of the hypotenuse is exactly \( \sqrt{2} \), so P is exactly \( \sqrt{2} \). Only the decimal 1.414 is an approximation.

intro: An irrational number like the square root of 2 is a real point on the number line. We can build it.
takeaways: Irrational numbers have exact places on the number line.
Pythagoras plus a compass turns √(k−1) into √k.
√2 ≈ 1.414 is only a decimal approximation of that exact point.

notes.title: Spiral of roots
notes.text: Repeating the construction gives √2, √3, √4, √5, … one after another. It is called the square root spiral.

challengeIntro: Now you try. Each question uses the picture above.
